findings.title: Design faithfully and proportionally implements slice-plan entry 915
findings.description: Every element the slice plan assigns is present and bounded: `scope: 'shared' | 'personal'` on `CONFIG_KEYS` with a required field (no silent default, consistent with project conventions), file routing absorbed inside `ConfigManager` with unchanged public signatures, the minimal one-line `cf init` gitignore addition (with the broader template explicitly deferred to the plan's Future Work item, which matches the plan verbatim), and the plan-mandated migration/compat story (read-time fallback, `ConsistencyChecker` detection, `migrate-personal` command). The design reuses the existing `readToml`/`resolveKey` merge machinery rather than inventing a new precedence mechanism, as the plan instructs. Nothing in the plan is dropped; no scope creep beyond it (the auto-fix exclusion is justified against the real `fixAction` type union). Effort matches the plan's 3/5, and the design explicitly resists extras (no dry-run flag, no interactive prompt).

findings.title: Failure modes and verification coverage are explicit for every new I/O path
findings.description: The migration path enumerates crash-between-steps handling (write-personal-then-delete-shared ordering, so failure leaves the key in both files, recoverable and idempotent), per-key failure continuation with `failed: <error>` reporting, collision semantics (absent/different/identical), write-failure semantics for the personal file (same helper, throws as today), and the `cf init` gitignore append failure (surfaced via existing `handleError`). None are "TBD". The verification walkthrough exercises the pre-migration fallback, detection, migration, and collision cases end to end, satisfying the parent architecture's "no behavior changes without tests" principle via the "existing tests pass unmodified in behavior" technical requirement.

findings.title: Delete routing spec contradicts the prescribed cleanup path for stale shared-file copies
findings.description: The Data Flow section specifies "**Delete:** mirrors write — deletes from whichever project file the key's scope maps to", and states `migrate-personal` is "the one exception that touches the *other* project file". For a personal key this means `cf config unset git.integration_branch --project` only touches `.context-forge.local.toml`. But the Collision semantics section (line 146) directs the user to clear a stale shared-file copy via "a separate, explicit `cf config unset <key> --project`", and Verification Walkthrough step 9 (line 259) asserts that this exact command clears the stale copy from `.context-forge.toml` and leaves `cf check` clean. Under the stated delete routing, step 9 is unreachable: `unset` would delete the *personal* copy (the developer's preferred value) while the stale shared copy survives the read fallback — inverting the intended outcome and leaving the `personal-config-in-shared-file` finding permanently unfixable by any documented command except hand-editing. The requirement left unmet is the design's own promised explicit cleanup path for the collision case. Fix: specify that project-scope delete for a personal key also removes any pre-existing copy in the shared file (read-side fallback mirrored on the delete side), or otherwise reconcile the two sections.

findings.title: "Reusing the pattern already used for personal ignores" has no referent
findings.description: Technical Scope says the `cf init` change works by "reusing the pattern already used for personal ignores", but the design's own `.gitignore handling in cf init` section (line 159) confirms "no gitignore-writing logic exists anywhere in `packages/cli`/`packages/core` today" — so there is no existing pattern to reuse. The normative section is self-contained and correct (create-if-absent, append-if-missing line check), so this is a wording issue only, but the phrase could send an implementer looking for scaffolding that does not exist.

structured_findings.summary: Design faithfully and proportionally implements slice-plan entry 915
Failure modes and verification coverage are explicit for every new I/O path
Delete routing spec contradicts the prescribed cleanup path for stale shared-file copies
"Reusing the pattern already used for personal ignores" has no referent
